note: Executable command authority for the EOS quality gate. An agent can choose a project and a suite, never a command. `%ENGINE%`, `%WORKSPACE%` and `%SELFTEST%` are the only path tokens; nothing here records a machine-specific absolute path. A suite with no verified entry point is marked NOT_CONFIGURED so the gate returns BLOCKED instead of a fake green.

pass.description: Self-test fixture that must pass. Proves the gate can return PASS.

fail.description: Self-test fixture that must fail. Proves the gate does not rubber-stamp.

mixed.description: One passing and one failing required command. Proves a single failure fails the suite.

optional_failure.description: Passing required command plus a failing optional one. Proves optional steps are recorded without blocking.

timeout.description: Proves a hung command is killed and reported, not waited on forever.

missing_binary.description: Proves a missing executable is a recorded failure, not an exception.

engine.description: Real behavioural suite of the product itself: a full skill-index rebuild followed by the router's routing scenarios, the activation plugin, and the orchestrator registry self-test.

security.description: Real secret scan over the engine. Fails if a credential-shaped string is committed in the product.

regression.description: Release and permission regressions. The release-gate self-test must reject forged PASS records, mismatched commits, changed gate registries, missing suites and tampered packages. The orchestrator runtime self-test must run real nested processes and prove depth, agent, step, timeout, cancellation and workspace bounds. The permission checks must prove no read-only role can write, delegate or bypass an external-directory denial.
